title: Choking and CPR Procedures
summary: Stepwise procedures for adult and infant choking, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and defibrillator (AED) use.
content:
1. ADULT CHOKING:
- Encourage coughing if the casualty can breathe or speak.
- If airway is completely blocked: Stand to the side and slightly behind. Support their chest with one hand, lean them forward, and deliver up to 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
- If unresolved, deliver up to 5 abdominal thrusts: Stand behind, place a fist above their navel, grasp with your other hand, and pull inward and upward sharply.
- Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts. Call 999 immediately if obstruction persists. If the casualty loses consciousness, start CPR.

2. INFANT CHOKING (UNDER 1 YEAR):
- Lay infant face down along your forearm, supporting their head and jaw with your hand.
- Deliver up to 5 gentle back blows between the shoulder blades.
- If unresolved, turn infant face up along your arm and give up to 5 chest thrusts using two fingers on the centre of the breastbone (compress 1/3 of chest depth). Never perform abdominal thrusts on infants.

3. ADULT CPR:
- Call 999 and put phone on speaker. Send someone to find a public defibrillator (AED).
- Place heel of one hand on centre of casualty's chest, interlock fingers of other hand on top.
- Press hard and fast: 5 to 6 cm deep at a rate of 100-120 beats per minute (to the beat of 'Stayin' Alive').
- Give 30 compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths (tilt head, pinch nose, blow until chest rises). If untrained or unable to give breaths, deliver hands-only continuous compressions.

4. PUBLIC DEFIBRILLATOR (AED): Open device lid or press power. Follow spoken voice prompts precisely. Attach pads to bare chest as illustrated. The AED will only deliver a shock if medically needed.
